source.title: MED-OPEN-001: open health-aid knowledge and medicine dossier provenance
source.body:
## Objective

Create a reusable, privacy-preserving governance and evidence model for open home health aids and open medicine dossiers across Mycelix, Symthaea, Sol Atlas, and Symtropy.

This is intentionally not a `mycelix-health` implementation task. It belongs in the public Mycelix platform as a domain-neutral provenance/governance contract and should integrate with existing manufacturing work rather than create a duplicate manufacturing runtime.

Related existing owners:
- Symthaea [HEALTH-MFG-000 #5969](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/issues/5969): evidence-bounded health-product manufacturing infrastructure.
- Symthaea [MED-PRODUCT-001 #4727](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/issues/4727): separate wellness and regulated intended-use profiles.
- Mycelix [MFG-001 #4685](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/mycelix/issues/4685): immutable manufacturing execution and lot evidence.
- Sol Atlas [ATLAS-DSCI-001 #99](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/sol-atlas-leptos/issues/99): licensed scientific evidence snapshots for open pharmaceutical research.
- Symtropy [MARITIME-SIM-001 #1612](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symtropy/issues/1612) and [ENG-SYNTH #1172](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symtropy/issues/1172): reuse deterministic engineering simulation/replay substrate for resilience scenarios.

## Scope

Separate four lanes that must never be collapsed into an AI-generated "safe" score:

1. **Open home-care knowledge:** authoritative, versioned first-aid, prevention and care-navigation material with jurisdiction, source, review/expiry, escalation language and correction/withdrawal paths.
2. **Non-medicinal household aids:** open assistive/accessibility designs, care-kit organization and low-risk tools, with materials and intended-use reviews.
3. **Existing medicine access:** link to authoritative medicine identities and local essential-medicine/availability information; preserve licensing, freshness, provenance and quality distinctions.
4. **Open medicine dossier:** public, reproducible scientific and quality documentation for appropriately authorized manufacturers and independent evaluators—product identity, applicable licenses/patents, test-method references, stability/packaging evidence, manufacturing-site qualification references, labeling, pharmacovigilance and recall.

Open licensing does not imply clinical validation, GMP compliance, product authorization, safety for unsupervised use, or permission to manufacture a medicine at home.

## Contract requirements

- Versioned content-addressed snapshot metadata; distinguish URL, publication date, retrieval date, source record identity, dataset version, bytes captured, digest verification, license/terms and redistribution permission.
- License states must include at minimum `KnownOpen`, `AttributionRequired`, `Restricted`, `Unknown`, and `ReviewRequired`. Publicly visible URLs do not grant redistribution rights.
- Preserve separate signed evidence dimensions for clinical benefit/harms, active/product identity and quality, analytical methods, stability, manufacturing capability/GMP, jurisdictional authorization, supply/affordability, safety-event status and recall.
- Use explicit lifecycle states and no implicit promotion: `ResearchOnly`, `SourceLinked`, `ReviewRequired`, `GuidanceApproved`, `ManufacturerQualified`, `ProductAuthorized`, `BatchDispositionRecorded`, `Withdrawn`, `Expired`. Applicable transitions need scoped evidence and accountable owners; states are not a linear clinical score.
- Append-only corrections, retractions, supersession, signing authority, conflicts, provenance edges, and reproducible evaluator receipts.
- Never store patient-identifying clinical data in public medicine dossier records. Separate consented private operational data from public, minimized evidence.
- Keep Mycelix responsible for provenance/authorization/evidence graphs, not for deciding clinical truth; keep clinical and regulatory decision authority with qualified organizations.

## Safety boundaries

No public at-home synthesis/compounding recipes, doses, extraction procedures, sterile/injectable/ophthalmic/inhaled preparations, potent or controlled actives, antibiotics, hormones or other high-risk medicine manufacturing instructions for unqualified users. Do not infer that “natural,” traditional use, an open license, low cost, model confidence or a successful simulation proves efficacy or safety. Traditional knowledge requires consent, rights review and fair benefit sharing.

## First deliverable

A public architecture document and minimal synthetic fixtures defining:
- `EvidenceSnapshotRefV1`
- `RightsAndLicenseAssessmentV1`
- `HealthKnowledgeCardV1`
- `OpenMedicineDossierManifestV1`
- `ProductEvidenceDimensionV1`
- `SafetySignalAndRecallRefV1`
- explicit claim ceiling / non-claims.

Use authoritative links rather than mirroring copyright-restricted clinical guidance. Seed South Africa from current official NDoH STG/EML references and WHO's 2025 Model List as pointers, subject to terms review. WHO says essential medicines should be available, affordable and of assured quality; its 2025 Model List includes over 520 medicines. NDoH's primary-care STG/EML page currently links an eighth-edition file last updated August 2026. Sources:
- https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/essential-medicines
- https://www.health.gov.za/nhi-edp-stgs-eml/
- https://www.sahpra.org.za/document/sa-guide-to-good-manufacturing-practice-for-medicines/
- https://medicinespatentpool.org/progress-achievements/licences

## Acceptance criteria

- Clear boundary between home care, existing-product access and qualified medicine production.
- Exact source and rights metadata without unauthorized corpus copying.
- No single composite evidence score; unresolved, restricted, withdrawn and expired states remain visible.
- Synthetic negative controls for license uncertainty, mismatched product/jurisdiction, stale evidence, retractions, conflicting evidence, unauthorized manufacturer, failed quality evidence and recall.
- Independent checker and exact-head reproducibility evidence.
- Link and reuse existing Mycelix manufacturing/provenance and Sol Atlas evidence semantics instead of creating competing authorities.
- Keep this work in Mycelix/Symthaea/Sol Atlas/Symtropy, not the separate Mycelix-Health application repository.

comments.author: Tristan-Stoltz-ERC
comments.text:
Initial cross-repository decomposition is now grounded in the existing project owners:

- **Mycelix:** [PR #5028](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/mycelix/pull/5028) proposes the reusable public evidence/right/provenance contracts and no-implicit-promotion lifecycle.
- **Symthaea:** existing [HEALTH-MFG-000 #5969](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/issues/5969), [MED-PRODUCT-001 #4727](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/issues/4727), and public-health epistemic ladder [#135](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/issues/135) own bounded synthesis, intended-use boundaries and uncertainty/abstention.
- **Sol Atlas:** existing [ATLAS-DSCI-001 #99](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/sol-atlas-leptos/issues/99) owns licensed source snapshots and access/geography projections. I added a note to keep source rights separate from scientific validity and to link rather than mirror NDoH/WHO documents until reuse terms are established.
- **Symtropy:** new [HEALTH-SUPPLY-SIM-001 #1617](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symtropy/issues/1617) uses the deterministic scenario/replay substrate for synthetic stockout, supplier disruption, lot quarantine/recall, transport, qualified second-sourcing and resilience-cost scenarios—not clinical predictions.

Research anchors:
- WHO Essential Medicines says products should be available, affordable and quality-assured: https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/essential-medicines
- South Africa's NDoH provides the STG/EML source page; treat it as a pointer until redistribution rights are established: https://www.health.gov.za/nhi-edp-stgs-eml/
- SAHPRA's current GMP guide is version 10 updated 24 April 2026; licensing guidance is version 4 updated 13 April 2026: https://www.sahpra.org.za/document/sa-guide-to-good-manufacturing-practice-for-medicines/ and https://www.sahpra.org.za/document/licence-to-manufacture-import-or-export/

The [Mycelix architecture PR #5028](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/mycelix/pull/5028) is documentation-only. Its exact-head D6S canonical qualification workflow is still queued at `7f3d9905f247bfc5a38072d3ac2bc3c5a468e4f4`; repository-wide CI was skipped for this docs-only path. No code or clinical claim is being represented as validated.

comments.author: Tristan-Stoltz-ERC
comments.text:
Implementation update — 14 October 2026:

The first executable source-rights slice is in [PR #5030](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/mycelix/pull/5030), extending the existing Mycelix-DeSci shared types crate instead of creating a new health application or parallel manufacturing runtime.

It adds `EvidenceSnapshotRefV1`, `RightsAndLicenseAssessmentV1`, and an operation-specific `evaluate_reuse` gate for metadata storage, full-artifact storage, redistribution, translation, commercial use and model training. The 18 authored synthetic tests cover unknown rights, missing per-operation grants, rights scoped to another source/version, digest receipt absence, expiry, future timestamps, attribution and deterministic blockers.

Important boundary: an unknown-rights source can remain referenceable, but that is explicitly not permission to copy or reuse its content. A license grant and a digest-verification receipt are separate inputs; neither proves scientific or clinical truth. This contract makes no clinical, regulatory, manufacturing or batch-release decision.

A focused exact-head workflow was added because the generic Mycelix CI intentionally skips draft PRs and the D6S workflow exercises an unrelated manufacturing reference. Current PR head: `d405629876e1dabf14e055f2f9d056c6af92d5ad`. The new [DeSci Source Rights Contract run 38617622387](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/mycelix/actions/runs/38617622387) is queued at that head; general [Mycelix CI run 38617622424](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/mycelix/actions/runs/38617622424) was skipped because the PR remains draft. Neither is a passing Rust test result, and local Rust tests were not run in this connector workflow.

Architecture and ownership remain as outlined in [PR #5028](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/mycelix/pull/5028): Mycelix owns evidence/rights/provenance, Symthaea owns bounded synthesis and abstention, Sol Atlas owns source-backed evidence projections, and Symtropy owns deterministic non-clinical supply-resilience scenarios.
